stem: Nora works in a government office. Section 3(g) of RA 6713 defines the "family" of a public official or employee. Which of these people is part of Nora's family under that definition?
hints: The definition in Section 3(g) is short. It names one kind of adult and one kind of child.
Section 3(g) says family means "spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age." A child must pass two tests.
For each child, ask two questions: Is the child unmarried? Is the child under 18? Only a child who passes both tests counts. Parents are not named in the definition.

solution.methodName: Check every condition in the definition

steps.action: Read Section 3(g): the family of public officials or employees "means their spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age."
steps.why: A spouse is a husband or wife. So the family is the spouse plus children who are both unmarried and below 18.

steps.action: Daughter, 19: she is unmarried, but she is not under 18. She fails the age test.
Son, 17: he is under 18, but he is married. He fails the unmarried test.
Mother, 70: parents are not named in Section 3(g).
steps.why: The law uses a separate, wider word, "relatives," in Section 3(k). "Family" and "relatives" are two different terms in RA 6713.

steps.action: Son, 16: he is unmarried and under 18, so he passes both tests. The answer is: Her unmarried son, aged 16.

trapNotes.Her unmarried daughter, aged 19: She is unmarried, but she is 19. Section 3(g) covers only children "under eighteen (18) years of age."
trapNotes.Her married son, aged 17: He is under 18, but he is married. Section 3(g) covers only "unmarried children."
trapNotes.Her widowed mother, aged 70: Section 3(g) defines family as only "spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age." A parent is not in that list.
